subject: Deployment mode & data residency — FinBank (EU/APAC) follow-up
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Müll er <sofia@finbank.eu>, Oliver Tan <oliver.tan@apacbank.sg>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@finbank.eu>
Date: 2027-06-30T13:12:00Z
Subject: Follow-up + next steps from today’s discovery — deployment mode & data residency

Hi Sofia / Oliver —

Thanks again for the call this morning — really helpful to understand the three main priorities across the EU and APAC teams. Quick recap and proposed next steps below.

Recap (from conversation):
- EU product team: strict requirement that EU customer data and PII must remain in EU. Primary priority is data residency and EU-only processing for EU customers.
- APAC product/security: low-latency for APAC customers; leaning toward a Private VPC or on-prem deployment in Singapore for highly regulated workloads.
- Procurement timeline: aiming for internal approvals by end of July.

Options we discussed (short):
1) Hosted API (Regional):
   - Pros: fastest time-to-value, no infra ops for you.
   - Cons: only viable if we can guarantee EU-only tenancy and region-level routing for EU traffic.
2) Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools in-region):
   - Pros: predictable throughput and single-tenant pools; can be isolated to EU regions.
   - Cons: commit-based pricing and lead time for provisioning.
3) Private (VPC / on-prem):
   - Pros: full network isolation, customer-managed networking, suitable for APAC on-prem/offline requirements.
   - Cons: longer lead time (sizing + networking + security review).

Questions / asks for you (so we can size next steps):
- Which jurisdiction is the priority to lock first (EU or APAC)?
- For EU: is Hosting (shared-hosted but EU-only tenancy) acceptable, or do you require Dedicated/Private?
- For APAC: is a Private VPC acceptable or do you require an on-prem appliance?
- Who on your security/compliance team should we loop in for SOC2 / ISO evidence?

Attachments: I’ve attached a short deployment options brief and a draft mutual action plan to help procurement + legal.

Next steps (proposed):
- You confirm priority (EU vs APAC) and the compliance contact.
- We schedule a 30-minute technical follow-up (I can bring Marissa from Solutions).
- I’ll share SOC2 summary + region availability matrix (attached).

Best,

Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: redwood-deployment-options.pdf, mutual-action-plan.xlsx

From: Sofia Müll er <sofia@finbank.eu>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@finbank.eu>, Oliver Tan <oliver.tan@apacbank.sg>
Date: 2027-06-30T14:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Follow-up + next steps from today’s discovery — deployment mode & data residency

Thanks Aditya — good summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- EU requirement: for EU customers we require that all customer data and derived artifacts (embeddings, logs) are stored and processed in the EU. A hosted option is acceptable only if you can guarantee EU-only tenancy and contractual commitments.
- APAC requirement: our Singapore product team is leaning toward Private VPC or on-prem; the main asks are network isolation and the ability to run within our Singapore region.
- Cross-region routing: can you confirm if EU-hosted traffic would ever route through a non-EU region for failover? Our compliance team will flag that.
- Compliance evidence: please share SOC2 Type II and ISO27001 summaries. Procurement copied here — we need pricing and a draft contract redline to hit the end-of-July timeline.

If we can get clear answers on EU tenancy and APAC Private options this week, procurement can move faster.

Best,
Sofia Müll er
Head of Product Security, FinBank
sofia@finbank.eu

Subject: Re: Follow-up + next steps from today’s discovery — deployment mode & data residency

Hi Sofia / team —

Thanks for the clarifying questions — answers inline below and attaching the region matrix + SOC2 summary for your review.

- EU tenancy guarantee: We can offer EU-only tenancy for hosted customers by routing and storing EU customer traffic entirely in our EU regions (data-subject-to-region policy + contractual commitment). For the highest assurance we recommend Dedicated capacity pinned to EU regions (single-tenant GPU pools).

- Cross-region routing / failover: Our smart routing can be configured with a strict region affinity policy so failover to non-EU regions does not occur for EU-tagged traffic. We also provide audit logs that show region and node-level processing if compliance needs to verify.

- APAC Private/VPC: We support Private VPC deployments in APAC (Singapore) — this is our recommended approach for the workloads you described. On-prem is also supported but requires a longer lead time and an engineering engagement for sizing. Typical lead time: 6–8 weeks for VPC setup; on-prem is 8–12 weeks depending on network approvals.

Attachments included: region-availability-matrix.csv, SOC2-Attestation-Redwood.pdf

Proposed next steps:
- Technical 30-min call with Marissa (Solutions) to confirm network/topology and confirm whether Hosted EU (with contractual EU-only commit) is sufficient vs Dedicated.
- Procurement: I’ll push a draft SOW + pricing this week once you confirm preferred deployment mode(s).

Available slots (PDT): Thu 2027-07-01 09:00, Fri 2027-07-02 10:30, Fri 2027-07-02 16:00. Let me know which works for the technical call and I’ll send a calendar invite.

Cheers,
Aditya

Attachments: region-availability-matrix.csv, SOC2-Attestation-Redwood.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Müll er <sofia@finbank.eu>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Procurement <procurement@finbank.eu>
Date: 2027-06-30T15:48:00Z
Subject: Re: Follow-up + next steps from today’s discovery — deployment mode & data residency

Hi Sofia / team — Marissa from Solutions here — looping in to confirm a couple of technical points and make the next steps concrete: 

1) Region availability: We currently operate Dedicated pools in eu-central-1 (Frankfurt) and eu-west-1 (Amsterdam). Hosted regional endpoints with EU-only tenancy are generally available today; Dedicated pools can be reserved and typically provision within 2–3 weeks depending on capacity at time of order.

2) Private VPC in APAC (Singapore): We can stand up a Private VPC in sg-1 with the network isolation you require. Lead time is typically 6–8 weeks because we need sizing input (TPS, peak tokens/min), transit/VPN setup, and customer security review. If you need an on-prem appliance, we’ll need a slightly longer procurement and engineering SLA.

3) Audit evidence: attaching a short SOC2 summary and an extract of our region routing policy for your compliance team. If needed, we can run a short architecture review call with your security stakeholders and provide tailored contractual controls (data processing addendum, data residency clause).

Next step proposal from Solutions:
- Let’s do the 30-min technical call this Friday 2027-07-02 at 10:30 PDT (17:30 CET). I’ll include a short runbook and the mutual action plan so procurement can track tasks.

Thanks — I’ll send the invite and include a brief agenda.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
